g.text: WMS + Dark Factory — Agentic Data Models, Risks, and the Fees That Block Agent Access
Workshop (human-led) vs factory (agent-led) vs lights-out: where the control lives when nobody is on shift, which records an agent may read, and what stops it today
THE WEAKEST LINK · NOT THE AI SWARM, THE PROCUREMENT DECISION
Plugin and SaaS data that crosses channels with no gate is the weakest link, not swarms of anthropomorphized AI bots
A form add-on that posts to the CRM, a base that syncs to Shopify, a zap that writes to the ERP: each was
bought for its features and its price, and each moves data between channels with no signature, no timestamp,
no escalation and no ledger. An agent doesn't create that path. It inherits it. Gate the crossing and the agent has
nothing more to reach; leave it open and no AI policy closes it.
Procurement gate · ask before buying
Does its data cross a channel, and through what transport?
Is every crossing signed, timestamped and logged?
Can a failure escalate into SAP, Dynamics, Salesforce or the WMS?
Scoped, expiring token, or one key to everything?
What happens at the rate limit, and how do we leave with our data?
LAYER
WORKSHOP · HUMAN-LED DEVOPS
FACTORY · AGENT-LED
DARK WAREHOUSE · LIGHTS-OUT
Who acts
A developer with their own login
Many agents in parallel, each with a workload identity
Robots, scanners and firmware fetching machine to machine; nobody on
shift
Main control
Human review: PR approval, click to deploy
Policy as code the pipeline enforces with no person
involved
A scoped, expiring mandate per task, checked on every call, revoked when
the shift ends
Identity
Long-lived user credentials, RBAC
Short-lived, scoped credentials or bindings for each task
Device attestation: the grant engine's fifth subject, beside invitation,
purchase, commission, agent
Where code runs
Developer laptop, shared CI
Isolated sandbox or VM for each agent run
A Worker isolate at the edge; credentials stay bindings, never with the
agent or robot
Blast radius
One person's mistake
One bad dependency or over-privileged agent, repeated
across every agent
A whole line or building: the highest blast radius in commerce
Evidence
Logs, plus whatever reviewers remember
Provenance and attestation (SLSA, SBOMs) recorded for
every artifact
A ledger row per scan and per call; EU CRA Art. 14 exploit reporting from
Main failure
Human error, credential theft
Prompt injection, privilege creep, a compromised supply
chain
Lookalike firmware, shared vendor VPN logins, last night's batch acted on
with confidence

svg.text: The workshop's controls don't vanish in a factory; they stop being gates, because the gate was the person, not the layer (LaunchDarkly). Treating the approval prompt as the control is the most common factory-security mistake (Warp). A lights-out site is the factory model
taken all the way: bindings, signed provenance, consent gates and edge policy are what still protect it.

g.text: AGENTIC DATA MODEL · AN AGENT RECEIVES ONE TASK, NOT ONE PLATFORM
Cloudflare binds, Xano grants, Rust checks, the WMS stays the system of record, and every yes and no leaves a ledger row
1 · Signed event
QR scan · EDI 856 · webhook
GS1 Digital Link on the item;
EventBridge, Pub/Sub or Service
Bus delivery
2 · Worker
Edge gate
checks the signature on the raw
body; idempotency key from the
event ID; holds every credential
3 · Xano grant
One task, as a row
record IDs, purpose, region,
expiry; revoke is a write, audit is a
read
4 · Rust check
Shape in, shape out
a tool the program doesn't declare
can't be constructed; typed
records only
5 · WMS / ERP
System of record
Blue Yonder (JDA), Manhattan,
SAP EWM, Dynamics;
unchanged, read by ID
6 · Ledger
Append-only
grant, task, bytes returned; the
evidence the CRA report needs
RECORDS AN AGENT MAY READ
Grant / mandate
Subject, task, record IDs, caps, purpose, region, expiry. The
grant ceiling is the injection ceiling: an agent can't be talked
into a tool it was never granted.
Envelope
An inert, searchable head (name, version, provenance,
licence, hash) and a payload behind a short-lived, per-grant
signed URL. Per-row keys: possession is not access.
Canonical unit record
Every measure once, as a UN/CEFACT code (KGM, MTR,
MTQ, KEL); WMS UoM mapped to it; GS1 AIs on everything
that ships; FX rate dated.
Transaction record
X12 850 / 856 / 810 typed by a Rust parser into JSON with a
published schema. The agent reads the record, never the
raw positional file.
RISK
HOW IT SHOWS IN A WMS OR DARK FACTORY
CONTROL
KNOWLEDGE BASE
Prompt injection
A label, ASN note or supplier PDF carries text an agent obeys
Tools declared in code, not in the prompt; grant scope enforced at the
data plane
Privilege creep
An ERP copilot runs as a service principal with ERP-wide roles
One task, listed record IDs, an expiry; renewals are new grants
Supply chain
Lookalike firmware or a poisoned dependency reaches every robot
Signing ceremony, published hashes, SBOM; attestation before fetch
Fleet blast radius
One over-permissioned agent copied across a fleet of pickers
Isolate per run, caps per grant, a kill switch that can only stop
Stale data
EDI daily windows, IDoc nightly runs, CDP 12–24 h refresh: the agent
answers from last night
Event in, row out, same cycle; IDs on the queue, not documents
Wrong shape
An LLM reads raw X12 or a vendor blob and guesses positions
Typed records with a schema; units converted at each surface's edge
Workaround backdoor
A transport blocked by JVM security rules is routed around with an
exception, shared drop or personal token; it multiplies across the
organization
One reinforced path for every tool: signed, timestamped, escalated,
logged; exceptions closed and audited
Can't see, can't report
CRA Art. 14: report actively exploited vulnerabilities from 11 Sep 2026
Ledger row per decision; evidence produced as a side effect
HUMAN IN THE LOOP · ESCALATION LADDER AND ENTERPRISE COMPLIANCE RISK
Automation may stop a crossing, but never approve one: the agent escalates on named conditions to a named role
0 · Run
Inside the grant
task, records, caps and expiry all match;
ledger row written
1 · Stop
Automatic, no person
a check fails or a cap is hit; the agent halts
and holds state
2 · Escalate
Named role, with a clock
quarantine, exception, new host, new field,
new purpose
3 · Decide
Approve, refuse, condition
a signed record with a review date; renewal
= new grant
4 · Report
Outside the company
CRA, GDPR breach, PCI or SOX evidence
from the ledger
ESCALATE WHEN
A pick, count or ship touches a record outside the grant's IDs
Personal, payment or health data appears where the purpose didn't list it
A device fails attestation, or firmware's hash isn't on the published list
Quantities, totals or units disagree between WMS, ERP and the EDI record
A model's answer would change a price, a credit, a refund or a person's account
ENTERPRISE COMPLIANCE RISK
WHAT THE HUMAN OWNS
GDPR Art. 22
decisions with legal or similar effect,
made solely by automation
a person able to review and overturn
EU AI Act Art. 14
human oversight for high-risk AI systems
an operator who can stop and override
SOX
change control and segregation of duties
on ERP data
approver separate from the author
PCI DSS v4.0
6.4.3 script inventory, 11.6.1 change
detection
authorising each payment-page script
EU CRA Art. 14
report actively exploited vulnerabilities
the report itself, from ledger evidence
SMALL BUSINESS → ENTERPRISE · CONTACT FORM 7, GRAVITY FORMS, MATRIXIFY, AIRTABLE, NOTION, ZAPIER
Suitable and effective for a small business. At enterprise scale they fail twice: at the rate-limit ceiling, and at security rules for JVM data transport
SMALL BUSINESS · USE THEM
ENTERPRISE · RATE-LIMIT CEILING
ENTERPRISE · JVM TRANSPORT BLOCKED
SAP · DYNAMICS · SALESFORCE · WMS: NO TIMESTAMP, NO ESCALATION
TOOL
SMALL BUSINESS: WHY IT WORKS
ENTERPRISE: RATE-LIMIT CEILING
ENTERPRISE: BLOCKED BY JVM TRANSPORT RULES
ENTERPRISE PATH
Contact Form 7
Free, simple, in the editor; a submission becomes an
email the owner reads
No queue or retry: one PHP request and one email
per submission; a spam flood or mail outage loses
leads
Email or an unsigned POST from shared hosting can't enter
middleware that requires mTLS, a signed payload and a
schema contract
POST to a Worker: Turnstile, MX, HMAC; Xano stores;
events out
Gravity Forms
Entries, conditional logic and add-on feeds without a
developer
Feeds call the CRM inside the same PHP request;
vendor API throttling drops or delays entries
Feeds leave from a hosting IP with no fixed egress or client
certificate, so the integration platform's allowlist rejects them
Same gateway; entries purged after hand-off
Matrixify
Whole-store bulk edits from a spreadsheet; the
fastest way to move a catalogue
Jobs queue behind Shopify Admin API limits; a large
file runs for hours and partial runs need reconciling
Files moved by hand, drive or FTP carry no signed
provenance or schema version; ERP and MDM intake won't
accept them
csv-gate, then Xano; productSet keyed by handle
Airtable · Notion
A shared workspace anyone can edit; views, forms
and simple automations
Per-base and per-integration request limits (Airtable
5 a second per base; Notion about 3) force polling
and exports
A long-lived token and an open polling connection to a
third-party SaaS fail egress policy; the connection can't be
reinforced
Read scopes; import to staging; Xano TLS transform
Zapier
No-code glue between hundreds of apps; running in
an afternoon
Task quotas per plan and polling intervals; volume
spikes stall or bill as overage
Shared multi-tenant IPs, a third party holding both ends'
credentials, and payloads kept in task history fail vendor
review
Signed events to a Worker; IDs, not records; ledger
SAP, Dynamics 365, Salesforce and the WMS can't take these updates with
A timestamp
Updates arrive with the tool's time, not the event's: a zap's run time, a CSV's export
time, Airtable's last-modified, an email's send time. SAP IDoc and OData,
Dataverse and Service Bus, Salesforce Platform Events and the WMS's ASN and
EDI feeds can't order them, can't settle a last-write conflict, and can't prove when
consent was given.
A security escalation
The tool has no channel to raise severity in the system of record. A failed check, a
suspicious row or a revoked token can't become an SAP block, a Dynamics
workflow, a Salesforce case or a WMS inventory hold; it stays an email or a failed
zap nobody owns.
The enterprise path
The Worker stamps event time, receipt time and an idempotency key; Xano keeps
the source and a ledger row; an escalation becomes a held record and a
named-role task; SAP, Dynamics, Salesforce or the WMS receives a signed event
carrying the timestamp and the status.
RISK · THE JVM BLOCKER BECOMES THE BACKDOOR
Blocked at the bus, teams route around it, and each workaround is a data transport with no reinforcement
CATASTROPHIC · LOSE EVERYTHING
1 · Blocked
The JVM bus rejects the tool: no mTLS, no signature,
no timestamp, no escalation
2 · Routed around
A broad service account, a firewall exception, a shared
FTP drop, a personal token in a zap, an emailed export
3 · Multiplied
Every team, tool and market adds its own path: tools ×
systems, each holding full-copy credentials
4 · One key, everything
One stolen token reaches SAP, Dynamics, Salesforce
and the WMS at once: catalogue, customers, orders,
stock

Why it's total: with no timestamp nobody can tell what changed or when, and with no escalation nobody was told, so there is no clean point to restore to and nothing to report. The fix is one reinforced transport every path must pass (Worker gate, Xano grant,
ledger) with the exceptions closed.

Why the ceiling becomes a security gap: the workaround for a rate limit is almost always another copy (a bulk export, a cache, one token shared across zaps, a retry that replays a payload). Fortify before the ceiling: keep the tool as the screen, move the record
behind the gate.

g.text: BUSINESS ANALYST BRIEF · TECH DEBT: SAAS FEE BLOCKERS FOR AI AGENT DATA ACCESS
The debt is in the contract, not the code: systems priced for people logging in now decide whether an agent may read
Most WMS, ERP, PIM and CRM subscriptions were priced per seat or per user. When an agent needs the same
data, the fee schedule, not the technology, sets whether it can have it and at what cost. Teams ration access,
export spreadsheets around the governed system, and the agent works from stale or partial copies. Each fee
blocker is technical debt with an interest rate: paid every month, and due at renewal.
SEAT
An agent must hold a licensed human
seat: automation billed at headcount
rates
METERED
Per API call or per record: the bill
rises as the automation is used
PREMIUM TIER
Real-time or hourly refresh sold as an
upgrade over a 12–24 h batch
ACCESS TERMS
Rate caps, AI add-on SKUs or
contract terms on automated access
COPY ONLY
Data reachable only as an export or a
vendor's own synced copy
What the analyst does
Inventory every system an agent must read: owner, pricing unit, renewal date, data residency
Ask in procurement: can an automated caller do this without a human seat, and what does 1,000 calls cost?
Price the capability, not the chair: one grant-scoped edge integration serves many agents
Log each blocker as debt with a payoff date, usually the renewal; compare BYO cost per call
Keep the vendor as system of record; move only the gate and the ledger. Coexistence, not replacement
